# ADR-039: Cross-model review for agent-authored changes

## Context

LLMs recognize and favor their own generations. When the same model family
both writes and reviews a change, the reviewer tends to read what the author
meant rather than what the diff says. This is the entire reason
danshapiro/fresheyes exists as a standalone tool: it routes review to the
opposite model family from the primary agent and reports that this catches
defects same-family review misses.

Today Lore's implementation and review agents resolve their model through the
same `lore.agent_definitions` chain (per-repo row, org-default row,
`task-types.yaml` fallback). Nothing prevents — and the defaults produce —
implementer and reviewer running on the same family. The autonomous review

# ADR-039: Cross-model review for agent-authored changes

## Amendment 2026-10-14: review shares the implementer's family

`code-review` and `code-review-recheck` run on `gemini-4-argon`, the same
family as the implementation loop's `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`; `code-review-reply`
stays on `claude-sonnet-4-6`. A local bench on five merged pull requests with
known must-fixes had Argon find all five that finished (one timed out) with no
false alarms, against four of six for Sonnet, plus a real bug neither Sonnet nor
the posted review caught (#2742). The catch rate outweighed the self-preference
risk this ADR names, so cross-family review is no longer a rule, only one input
to the model choice. The cost: Argon is about three times slower (review timeout
25 min, re-check 20) and about 40% dearer …

## What Changed

**The policy helpers** — `libs/shared/src/llm/model-family.ts`:

- `modelFamily(id)` classifies a model id into `anthropic` / `openai` / `google`, returning **`unknown` rather than guessing** for anything it cannot place. Handles the id forms a real cross-provider setup produces: bare ids, Bedrock (`anthropic.claude-…`, `us.anthropic.claude-…`), OpenRouter (`openai/gpt-5`), the OpenAI o-series (`o3`, `o4-mini`, `o1-preview`), `chatgpt-*`, and untrimmed input.
- `crossModelReviewWarning(implementer, reviewer)` returns a warning when both resolve to the same family, with a sharper message for the identity case (one model grading its own output — where self-preference is strongest).

**A guard against the next model** — a test iterates the real `KNOWN_MODELS` array (the Agent…

# ADR-039: Cross-model review for agent-authored changes

## Decision

The org-default `agent_definitions` row for review-type agents pins a model
from a different family than the implementation default. Concretely: while
the implementation default resolves to the Anthropic/Claude family, the
review default is pinned to OpenAI's current flagship (`gpt-5.6` at time of
writing), and vice versa. When an implementation task's model is overridden
per-repo, the repo owner is responsible for keeping the review model
cross-family; the settings UI surfaces a warning when implementer and
reviewer resolve to the same family.

**Prerequisites.** The ai-agent-subsystem's `claude-code` vendor only calls
the Anthropic API today, so cross-provider review is not yet reachable by
row edits alone: the subsys…
